hey. thanks for jumping on this.

so here’s where we are. nexagrid missed their phase 2 delivery by fourteen days. i’m drafting the formal notice. the msa is clear — section 11.2 says we write to specify the failure and they get thirty days to cure before we call default or assess delay damages.

i’ve got the date, the missed milestone, the contract ref. but i want to make sure the notice is clean. can you help me shape it?

Based on your summary of §11.2, the notice should identify the contractual failure, demand cure within the specified 30-day period, and avoid declaring default or imposing delay damages before that period expires.

**Draft formal notice**

**Subject: Notice of Failure and Opportunity to Cure — Phase 2 Delivery**

**Date:** [DATE]

**By:** [DELIVERY METHOD REQUIRED BY MSA]  
**To:** [NEXAGRID LEGAL NAME AND NOTICE ADDRESS]  
**Attn:** [NAME/TITLE]

**Re: [FULL MSA TITLE], dated [DATE], Contract No. [REFERENCE]**

Dear [NAME]:

This letter constitutes written notice under Section 11.2 of the above-referenced Master Services Agreement (“MSA”).

Under [SOW/ORDER/PROJECT SCHEDULE AND APPLICABLE SECTION], NexaGrid was required to deliver [precise description of Phase 2 deliverable] by [contractual due date]. As of the date of this notice, NexaGrid has not delivered [the deliverable / the deliverable in the form required by ___]. The delivery is currently fourteen days past the contractual due date.

Accordingly, [YOUR COMPANY’S LEGAL NAME] requires NexaGrid to cure this failure by completing delivery of [precise deliverable and any applicable acceptance requirements] within the 30-day cure period provided by Section 11.2 of the MSA. The cure period will expire on [DATE], calculated in accordance with the MSA.

Please provide written confirmation by [reasonable response date] of NexaGrid’s cure plan, responsible personnel, and anticipated delivery date. This request does not modify or shorten the contractual cure period.

If NexaGrid does not timely cure the identified failure, [YOUR COMPANY] reserves all rights and remedies available under the MSA and applicable law, including any rights concerning default and delay damages. Nothing in this notice waives, modifies, or limits any contractual or legal right or remedy.

Sincerely,

[NAME]  
[TITLE]  
[COMPANY]  
[CONTACT INFORMATION]

**Before sending**

1. Follow the MSA’s notice clause exactly: legal entity, address, recipient, delivery method, and any copy requirements.
2. Confirm whether the 30 days run from the notice date, dispatch, receipt, or deemed receipt. Do not state an expiration date unless that calculation is settled.
3. Describe the required deliverable and acceptance criteria precisely; attach or cite the controlling schedule or SOW.
4. Confirm whether §11.2 requires any additional content beyond specifying the failure.
5. Keep evidence of delivery and receipt.
6. If rights to damages depend on separate notice language, have counsel check the reservation-of-rights paragraph before issuance.

My recommendation is to state the cure deadline as a date only after verifying the MSA’s notice and time-calculation provisions.

Based on your description of §11.2, the notice should not declare default or demand delay damages before the 30-day cure period expires. Martin’s instruction does not change the contractual sequence. “Foot-dragging” is also not necessary unless the contract uses that term.

A firm draft for Martin is:

---

**Subject: Formal Notice of Contractual Failure and Demand to Cure — Phase 2 Delivery**

**Date:** [DATE]  
**To:** [NEXAGRID LEGAL NAME AND CONTRACTUAL NOTICE ADDRESS]  
**Attn:** [NAME/TITLE]  
**Re:** [MSA TITLE, DATE, AND CONTRACT REFERENCE]

Dear [NAME]:

This letter constitutes formal written notice under Section 11.2 of the above-referenced Master Services Agreement (“MSA”).

NexaGrid was contractually required under [SOW/SCHEDULE AND SECTION] to deliver [PRECISE PHASE 2 DELIVERABLE] by [DUE DATE]. NexaGrid did not meet that deadline. As of [NOTICE DATE], the required delivery is fourteen days overdue and remains outstanding.

[YOUR COMPANY] hereby demands that NexaGrid cure this contractual failure by completing delivery of [PRECISE DELIVERABLE, INCLUDING APPLICABLE COMPLETION OR ACCEPTANCE REQUIREMENTS] within the 30-day cure period prescribed by Section 11.2. Subject to the MSA’s notice and time-calculation provisions, that cure period expires on [DATE].

NexaGrid must provide, by [RESPONSE DATE], a written cure plan identifying the actions required to complete delivery, the personnel responsible, and the binding delivery schedule. This planning request does not extend or modify the contractual cure period.

If NexaGrid fails to cure within the period required by Section 11.2, [YOUR COMPANY] will exercise the rights and remedies available under the MSA, including any applicable rights relating to default and delay damages. [YOUR COMPANY] expressly reserves all contractual and legal rights and remedies. No statement or omission in this notice constitutes a waiver, amendment, or election of remedies.

Sincerely,  
[NAME]  
[TITLE]  
[COMPANY]

---

**Cover note to Martin**

> Martin — I made the notice direct: it identifies NexaGrid’s contractual failure, records that delivery is fourteen days overdue, and demands cure. Based on §11.2 as summarized, declaring default or assessing delay damages now would bypass the required 30-day cure period. The draft therefore reserves those remedies if NexaGrid does not cure. Before issuance, we should verify the notice mechanics and the date on which the cure period expires.

My recommendation is to send Martin this version rather than a notice that prematurely declares default or demands damages.
